Unless the context otherwise requires, references in this MD&A section to “Wheels Up,” “we,” “us,” “our,” and “the Company” are intended to mean the business and operations of Wheels Up Experience Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries for all periods.

We are focused on growing our premium jet fleet to meet expected future demand, including through the order of six (6) factory-new Embraer Phenom 300E premium jets that we expect will be delivered in the third and fourth quarters of 2027.

On November 3, 2026, we took our latest step to align long-term fleet expansion with anticipated member and customer demand by entering into a purchase agreement with Embraer (the “Phenom Purchase Agreement”) to acquire six (6) factory-new Phenom 300E premium business jet aircraft, which are expected to be delivered in the third and fourth quarters of 2027.
These aircraft are expected to supplement our growing fleet of Embraer Phenom 300 and 300E premium jets, and meaningfully contribute to our operations over the long-term.
We also expect to continue opportunistically adding Bombardier Challenger 300 and 350 premium jets in 2027 to service expected membership and charter demand.

We first announced in August 2025 that we were in the process of implementing initiatives expected to drive approximately $50 million in annual cash cost savings through efficiency, productivity and overhead cost reduction actions associated with our fleet modernization plan and other strategic plans.

While a portion of the savings that we originally expected from such actions are reflected in our results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, we anticipate that the full impact of the anticipated cost savings and control actions will be reflected in our financial results by the end of 2026 relative to a second quarter of 2025 baseline.
In September 2026, we announced that an enhanced Sustainable Aviation Fuel (“SAF”) program will be our primary sustainability offering, replacing our previous carbon offsetting program.

The Company expects to use any amounts borrowed under the 2026 Revolving Credit Facility for working capital and general corporate purposes, including to execute the Company’s ongoing business transformation, continue investing in its premium jet fleet and/or repay existing indebtedness, and to pay certain transaction-related expenses.

These decreases were partially offset by an $84.9 million increase in third-party operator spend due to shifting certain flight activity to third-party operators as we scaled down and retired our legacy fleets from revenue service during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a $8.8 million increase in aircraft lease costs and $4.9 million of legacy fleet retirement-related costs not present in our results for…

We expect to meet our liquidity needs for the next 12 months with a combination of cash and cash equivalents, cash flows from operations, strategic dispositions of legacy aircraft, proceeds from borrowings under the Revolving Equipment Notes Facility, 2023 Revolving Credit Facility and 2026 Revolving Credit Facility, as needed, and, depending on market conditions, sales of shares of Common Stock or other debt or…

In addition, as of September 30, 2026, scheduled maturities of our long-term debt were expected to be approximately: (i) $5.9 million for the remainder of 2026; (ii) $92.9 million for 2027; (iii) $660.1 million for 2028; and (iv) $250.7 million for 2029.

As of September 30, 2026, the Series A Equipment Notes and Series B Equipment Notes were secured by senior liens on 44 and 40, respectively, of our owned aircraft and in the future will be secured by senior liens on additional aircraft financed under the respective facilities (collectively with the PDP Collateral (as defined below), the “Revolving Equipment Notes Collateral”).

As we continue to scale our premium jet fleet, we anticipate, among other things, making investments to grow our fleet and operations, which may include purchasing or leasing aircraft, acquiring other private aviation businesses or entering into alternative financing structures or business arrangements to provide aircraft supply or grow our charter solutions platform.
We expect our next phase of growth will be capital intensive and require significant internal and external resources.

As of the date of this Quarterly Report, we expect that we will fund any fleet-related obligations or commitments using cash and cash equivalents on-hand, including cash proceeds received from any sales or sale-leaseback transactions involving our controlled aircraft or other assets, operating cash flows, available borrowings under the Revolving Equipment Notes Facility, 2023 Revolving Credit Facility and 2026…
We expect to fund sale and lease return expenses as part of our normal business operations utilizing available liquidity or proceeds from future financings.
